That section excludes only two distinct positive values of g; it never excludes negative values. Although (3) can be iterated to obtain f^n(t)=t+n(f(t)-t), whose positivity for every n forces g(t)≥0, this induction and conclusion are absent. Thus V could, based on the established statements, contain negative values, so the assertion that every point lies in S_0∪S_c is unjustified. Lemma 1 and the subsequent covering argument explicitly rely on g(z)∈{0,c}, so the missing nonnegativity step is load-bearing and leaves the upper-bound/necessity proof incomplete as written."}
